event: Zadi tells them to sit: it's soup, and bread she didn't make, the whole menu.
Natalie isn't sitting, she's looking: that's not just soup. Zadi: leeks; the recipe knew.
Amy asks where the bread goes; Zadi points her to the other board.
Natalie brought the honey, as she said she would: for the bread, not the soup.
Zadi asks why she'd put honey in soup; Amy says she might've; Zadi says she would not.
Amy brought the labels too, just in case.
Zadi: her pantry doesn't want to be trustworthy; it likes keeping a couple of secrets.
Amy: last time it had two open bags of the same flour. Zadi: a surplus, not a secret.
Natalie tastes it: this is actually good, Zadi.
Zadi asks if it is; Natalie tells her not to do that, she knows it is.
Zadi only hoped: you can't tell with soup till someone else eats it. Amy: it's good.
Natalie reaches for the ladle; Zadi says sit.
Natalie is only reaching; Zadi: her table, she gets to say it. Sit.
Natalie: well, now, would you look at that.
Amy: she's saved that a whole month. Zadi: a month exactly, since Natalie's table.
Zadi wrote it down; Natalie doubts it; Zadi: mentally.
Natalie asks the boss to pass the honey; Zadi hands it over: Natalie brought it.
It's from the man past the feed store, hives behind the tree line, no labels on any jar.
You point at a jar and he tells you its field; this one is late clover.
Natalie couldn't tell clover from anything, but believed him.
Amy says he should label them; Natalie: half the point is the man telling you.
Amy offers to bring him labels; Zadi forbids it; Natalie says leave him be.
The honey runs in the good way on the warm bread.
Amy: store bread holds honey tighter and doesn't soak.
The bread is the corner place's sourdough from the window.
Zadi isn't proud: she knows her one thing, and it's soup.
Amy calls knowing your one thing underrated; Zadi says write that down.
Amy doesn't write things down; Natalie: she just remembers everything, a little unsettling.
The soup is Zadi's aunt's recipe; she made it only for people she liked.
Zadi felt very chosen, growing up, getting a bowl.
Natalie: that's the best kind of soup there is.
Zadi called her aunt to get it right, and all she'd say was: you'll know.
Natalie: that's her grandmother's cards exactly.
Does she ever know? Eventually, after the brick and the sponge.
Zadi has picked her next book; the audition is over.
It's the blue one: she doesn't know what it's about, but liked its weight in her hand.
Natalie: she picks books like produce. Zadi: everything; squeeze it, smell it, trust it.
Amy: that explains the pantry. Zadi: leave her pantry out of it, Amy's a guest.
Amy asks whose month is next.
Natalie: "We did mine, then Zadi's—" so it's Amy.

memory.fact: Natalie hosted the first of those suppers, with Amy and Zadi as her guests.

event: Amy: it's her, and she's been ready since spring.
Zadi: they'll all be using coasters. Amy: Zadi will.
Natalie bets she has a diagram already; Amy: there's a diagram, and a whole plan.
Amy offers more soup while it's hot; Zadi takes half, a little bit.
Natalie is slowing down after starting strong; she went in hard on the bread.
She'd do it again; Zadi: there's more if the regret shows up later.
Natalie: it always shows up later; that's what later's for.
Natalie's tomatoes are done; she pulled the last of them this week.
The intensive-care tomatoes pulled through, and then they quit, like anybody does.
She has greens going in now, cool-weather things to fuss over through the fall.
Zadi: she just likes having something out there to talk to.
Natalie likes something that listens, no offence; Amy: none taken, she wasn't listening.
Zadi asks if that's thyme in the soup; Amy was about to ask.
It came in a bundle and Zadi used the whole bundle.
Zadi doesn't measure herbs, she's not a chemist; Amy does, and hers come out even.
Natalie notes the candles are getting low; Zadi: let them.
Natalie likes them like this, down to the last steady bit. Zadi: the part that's just glow.
Zadi remembers the promised poem: before anybody leaves, she won't let it slide.
It's short and traditional, from her grandmother's side; she gropes for how it starts.
Natalie tells her to take her time, sugar.
"The day is done and wants for nothing. The bread is cut, the lamp is low."
"The last of the light goes soft and blue, and the evening keeps the door."
Natalie: that's a nice one, good to have by heart; Amy likes it.
It's the only poem Zadi has by heart; that's how it got the job.
A heel of bread is unclaimed; Amy is done, happily; Zadi: it'll be somebody's breakfast.
Natalie offers to lid the honey; Zadi likes knowing it's there.
Zadi isn't moving for a while; Natalie: sit as long as you want, it's your table.
Amy: the whole room's gone amber. Zadi: it does that, this hour.
Zadi will get the candles; Natalie: in a minute. Zadi: in a minute.
